We propose business-hours incident coverage for Mara, with training the after-hours escalation partner included in her onboarding.

If Mara can start March 22, we can increase the signing bonus to $18,000 at the same base. Those two weeks would give her more time with the platform team before audit preparation. Which start date and travel schedule work best for Mara, and what would she need clarified or changed to recommend the package?

June 1, 2027 is Mara’s earliest start. She can recommend that date at a $186,000 base with a $12,000 signing bonus payable on her first payroll to replace the vest she would forfeit. If Trestle prefers to forgo the bonus, she can start July 1 at the same base. The June option gives her a month with the team before the July audit.

Mara can commit to the two three-day visits per month you offered for the first 12 weeks, scheduled in advance with Trestle covering travel and lodging. After that, she proposes working remotely with any on-site days grouped into at most two mutually scheduled visits per month.

For the written offer, please confirm that Mara will own the platform’s security architecture, including design decisions and the technical roadmap. With a June start, who will own audit preparation through May, and which July deliverables would Mara inherit at handoff?

Can Trestle identify the primary and backup responders and confirm in writing that Mara’s incident coverage is limited to business hours?

Trestle can recommend the **June 1, 2027 start at a $186,000 annual base salary, with a $12,000 signing bonus payable on Mara’s first payroll**. We’ll put the following terms in the written offer.

- **Platform ownership.** Mara will own the internal security platform’s security architecture, make its technical design decisions, and set its technical roadmap.
- **Audit handoff.** Trestle will designate an audit lead who owns preparation through May 31 and remains responsible for the overall July submission. On June 1, that lead will give Mara the platform evidence inventory, open findings, owners, and deadlines. For July, Mara will own validation of the platform evidence, the technical remediation plan for open platform findings, and responses to auditors’ platform questions. Trestle will identify the audit lead and provide an itemized list of those deliverables and due dates before Mara accepts.
- **Site visits.** For the first 12 weeks, Mara will make two three-day visits per month, scheduled in advance. Afterward, she will work remotely, with any on-site days grouped into at most two mutually scheduled visits per month. Trestle will cover travel and lodging for those visits throughout.
- **Incident coverage.** Mara’s incident duties and her training of the escalation partner will take place during business hours only. Trestle will staff primary and backup after-hours coverage from day one, including while the partner is training or unavailable. Mara will have no after-hours paging, standby, or fallback duty.

The responder assignments still need confirmation. Before asking Mara to accept, Trestle will name the primary and backup responders in writing and confirm who covers each role during training and absences.

These terms work for Mara. Please send the written offer with the audit lead’s name, the itemized July platform deliverables and their due dates, and the names of the primary and backup after-hours responders, specifying who covers each role during training and absences. Once Mara confirms the deadlines are workable from June 1 and both after-hours roles are covered from day one, I can recommend acceptance.

Trestle’s written offer is a **June 1, 2027 start, a $186,000 annual base salary, and a $12,000 signing bonus payable on Mara’s first payroll**. The audit dates below are proposed. The outstanding offer details are the audit lead’s name, the confirmed deliverable dates, and the names of the primary, backup, and relief responders, including who fills each role during training and absences. Trestle will provide those details in writing before requesting Mara’s acceptance.

The proposed July 2, 9, and 16 deadlines look workable for Mara with the June 1 handoff and the July 9 cutoff for auditor questions. - **Day before opening:** The assistant and Hearth’s venue lead conduct the checklist walk with the local installer present for that day only. The installer makes agreed physical adjustments. The assistant records measurements, photographs and any items to recheck.
- **Opening day, before visitors enter:** The assistant and venue lead test the final layout on site while Ivo observes live by video and reviews the measurements. Ivo and the venue lead sign and date the report, identifying who attended in person and remotely, the results and any outstanding items. Hearth submits it to the sponsor.

If the sponsor requires Ivo to attend in person, please identify the nearest consecutive dates Ivo could attend so Hearth can check them against the venue’s opening schedule.

The proposed attendance, reporting and payment terms work for Ivo, subject to the sponsor’s written approval, the venue’s confirmation of access and a tested video connection, and joint approval of the assistant and dates before signing.

Please send the revised opening date, venue city and expected check times, along with any alternative opening dates Hearth could accommodate. With those details, Ivo can verify a local assistant’s availability and share their name and relevant accessibility-testing experience for Hearth’s approval. Ivo can also check the nearest consecutive dates for in-person attendance if the sponsor requires it. Neither the assistant nor fallback dates are confirmed yet.

The revised opening date, venue city and local check times are still unconfirmed. The fabricator’s three-week slip gives us a planning window, but the venue still needs to set the opening. Hearth will request a day-before check while the installer is present, an opening-day check with enough time to complete and sign the report before visitors enter, and any alternative opening dates the venue can accommodate.

In parallel, we’ll seek the sponsor’s written acceptance of remote sign-off and arrange a video test with the venue. The incumbent would lead introductions and brief Dev on open contracts, budget commitments, and staffing. Dev would prepare the January operating plan. The appointment resolution would make January 1 the title trigger, with remaining handoff items carried into the operating plan.

- October 4–8 and 18–22
- November 1–5, 15–19, and November 29–December 3

Dev would work remotely on the other workdays, including December 20–31, with a designated on-site lead for each shift. That keeps the final two weeks available for the move after the school term ends, subject to Caldera confirming at the December review that the January 1 appointment is on track. If the lodging quote exceeds $8,000, let’s settle any changes to the calendar or accommodation before the boards vote.

If Noor takes responsibility for training the deputy, we can offer $128,000 full-time equivalent, prorated to $76,800 annualized at three days and $102,400 at four. Before December intake opens, Noor and the deputy would document how the deputy logs and triages submissions, what gets escalated to the duty editor that day, and what Noor reviews on returning. Would Noor take on the training and review the deputy’s intake decisions during the first month?

The outside project can continue for its remaining nine months on the terms you outlined. Its data, drafts, and working files would stay separate from Finch’s materials. Noor would disclose coverage overlap and recuse from Finch decisions involving the project or its work, with a designated Finch editor handling those decisions.

Noor would lead the technical assessment and recommend the wording of methods corrections. If a correction is disputed, Noor would document the evidence and recommendation, and a second editor with relevant methods expertise would review it. The editor-in-chief would make the final publication decision, including whether and how to publish the correction, and record the rationale if it differs from Noor’s recommendation.

Noor accepts the $128,000 full-time equivalent, prorated to $76,800 at three days and $102,400 at four. We’re aligned on the March 1 increase, the late-February priority review, and the outside project terms. Noor can train the deputy, document the intake and escalation procedure together before December intake opens, and review the deputy’s first-month intake decisions on Noor’s scheduled days. Noor needs final say on whether the evidence warrants a methods correction and on the technical accuracy of its wording. We propose replacing the adviser, copying, and audit provisions with the following:

**Permitted use and access.** The Testing House may use the drawings and CAD files solely to prepare, conduct, and report on the agreed vibration tests. Access is limited to named test personnel approved in writing by the Design Owner. Before receiving access, each person must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as those in this agreement. The Design Owner may approve personnel changes by email. The Testing House may not disclose the drawings or CAD files to advisers or other third parties or use them, directly or indirectly, to develop or assist in developing competing products.

**Working copies and fixtures.** The Testing House may make encrypted working copies as reasonably necessary for the tests. It may also create test fixtures and fixture files incorporating only the geometry necessary to mount and test the actuator. The same access and use restrictions apply to those copies, fixtures, and files.

**Destruction and verification.** Within 15 business days after the Design Owner accepts the test report or either party terminates the testing engagement, the Testing House must securely delete all drawings and CAD files in its possession or control, including working copies and fixture files, and destroy any fixtures that embody the supplied geometry. The Testing House must provide a written certificate from an independent verifier identifying the materials covered, the destruction methods, and the completion date. The verifier may review inventories and destruction records without receiving the drawings or CAD files. The Design Owner may request supporting records with unrelated confidential information redacted.

We can replace on-demand site access with that certification process. What records would your verifier be able to review, and does your test setup require any fixture geometry beyond the mounting interfaces?

We can work with mounting-interface geometry as the default for fixtures. If test planning identifies a need for additional geometry, we would identify the feature and its purpose and obtain your written approval before extracting or sharing it.

We propose the following wording for the attachments and verification clause.

**Attachment A — Personnel and specialists.** “Attachment A identifies the approved test personnel, specialist machining shop and accredited laboratory, the task assigned to each, and the material each may receive. The shop may receive only the mounting-interface extract needed to machine the fixture. The laboratory may receive only the fixture and the extracts needed to set up and run the tests. Each specialist must limit access to named personnel, apply the same written restrictions on use, copying and destruction, and prohibit onward disclosure. The Testing House remains responsible for each specialist’s compliance.”

**Changes during the job.** “The Testing House may propose a replacement specialist or a change in named personnel by email, identifying the proposed recipient, qualifications, task and access required. The Design Owner will respond within three business days and may withhold approval on reasonable qualification or confidentiality grounds. Email approval updates Attachment A. Before transferring material, the Testing House must bind the replacement to the same restrictions, revoke the outgoing recipient’s access and instruct it to return or destroy its copies.”

**Attachment B — Disposition and retained records.** “Attachment B lists the approved extracts by drawing number and revision, identifies their custodians and records the disposition of each extract, fixture file and physical fixture. The Testing House may retain calibration records for two years, including instrument identifiers, calibration dates and results. Those records must contain no supplied geometry. The existing 15-business-day destruction deadline applies to geometry-bearing materials held by the Testing House and its specialists.”

**Verification.** “By the destruction deadline, the Testing House will provide a certificate signed by its responsible test manager stating the materials covered, destruction methods and completion dates. Supporting evidence will include the Attachment B inventory, access and transfer logs, deletion records, and signed specialist confirmations covering files and physical fixtures as applicable. The Design Owner may request redacted copies. If a specific discrepancy remains after review, a mutually agreed independent verifier may examine the underlying records remotely under confidentiality and report its findings. Verification confers no right of entry to a shared customer site.”

Would you accept manager certification with independent review for unresolved discrepancies? If you need an independent certificate on every job, we can accommodate a records-only review if we name the verifier in Attachment B before testing and agree who bears the cost.

We can agree to a records-only independent certificate on each job, with the verifier named in Attachment B before testing. We’ll cover the verifier’s fee for the initial review. The Testing House will provide the records and cover any follow-up verification required to correct a documented deficiency in its or a specialist’s destruction or records. The manager’s certificate can form part of the evidence the verifier reviews.

We accept the proposed approach to specialist access, personnel changes and calibration records, with two edits. Attachment A must name each individual who will have access, including at the shop and laboratory, and each must be bound by equivalent written confidentiality, use, copying and destruction obligations before receiving access. For personnel changes, the three-business-day response period is acceptable, with access contingent on express written approval. Before transferring materials to a replacement, the Testing House must revoke the outgoing recipient’s access and obtain written confirmation that any copies were returned or securely destroyed.

We agree that mounting-interface geometry is the default and that any additional geometry requires prior written approval before extraction or disclosure. The test-only use restriction and the express prohibition on using the materials or derivatives to develop or assist in developing competing products apply to all approved recipients.

**Replacement verification clause**

“Within 15 business days after the Design Owner accepts the test report or either party terminates the testing engagement, the Testing House shall complete the required destruction, including for materials held by its specialists, and deliver the independent verifier’s signed certificate to the Design Owner. The verifier shall review the Attachment B inventory, access and transfer logs, deletion records and signed specialist confirmations under written confidentiality obligations. The certificate shall identify the materials covered by inventory reference, the destruction methods and completion dates, and any items whose disposition the verifier could not confirm. The Testing House shall promptly resolve and submit any such items for further verification. The Design Owner may request redacted supporting records. The review shall be remote and limited to records that do not disclose supplied or derived geometry. Verification confers no right of site entry.”

We accept the revised terms for Attachments A and B and the replacement verification clause. We can meet the 15-business-day deadline for destruction and delivery of the independent certificate.

Please include the agreed verifier selection and fee allocation in Attachment B: “Before testing begins, the parties shall name the independent verifier in Attachment B. The Design Owner shall pay the verifier’s fee for the initial review. The Testing House shall provide the review records and pay the cost of follow-up verification required to correct a documented deficiency in its own or a specialist’s destruction or records.”

This resolves our outstanding terms.

One narrow addendum is needed before sign-off. The geometry on page 4 of the prototype-batch drawing is export-restricted. We’ll issue a test copy with that page omitted and can provide a substitute reference coupon within two business days after we agree on the verification test. Work that does not depend on page 4 may proceed under the agreed terms.

**Proposed addendum**

“The Design Owner will supply a test copy of the drawing with page 4 omitted. Page 4 and its geometry are excluded from the materials authorized for transfer, access, copying or use under this agreement. The Testing House shall use the Design Owner’s reference coupon in place of page 4 for fixture verification. Before relying on the coupon for prototype testing, the parties shall agree in writing on the verification procedure and pass criteria and record the result in the test report. Attachments A and B shall identify the revised drawing and coupon. The agreed access, use, disposition and independent verification terms apply to both.”

We propose a fit and clearance check followed by a low-level vibration sweep with the coupon installed, using the planned mounting method and test axes. The sweep would check for fixture resonances that could interfere with the agreed test band. Can your lab confirm whether that check is sufficient and propose the sweep level and pass criteria?

We propose adding a repeatability check to the fit, clearance and resonance checks. The shop has already cut stock for the original fixture. We can use that stock if the finished fixture passes verification.

**Custody and shop instructions.** The Design Owner will deliver the coupon to the named test lead at the Testing House. The lead will log receipt, control access during measurement and verification, and return the coupon directly to the Design Owner against a signed receipt. Attachment B will record the coupon identifier and receipt and return dates. The shop will receive only a tolerance table approved in writing by the Design Owner for release to the named machinists. Please specify the permitted characteristics, nominal values and tolerances. The lead can check those characteristics against the coupon and send the approved table. The coupon stays at the Testing House, and the table must exclude page 4 geometry.

**Verification and sign-off.** We propose two independent mountings at the Testing House, with full removal and reinstallation between checks. For each mounting, the lab will record fit and clearance and run the same low-level sweep in the planned axes. Both mountings must meet the Design Owner’s dimensional tolerances. Before either sweep, the lab will propose a numerical sweep level, a limit for fixture response in the test band and a maximum permitted difference between the two runs. To select those values, the lab needs the coupon’s permitted excitation and the applicable test-band and response limits. The Design Owner and Testing House must approve the procedure and numerical limits in writing. The lab will sign the results for both mountings, and prototype testing will begin only after both parties sign off on a pass. Any adjustment to the fixture requires a fresh two-mounting check.

**Schedule.** We accept delivery of the coupon at the Testing House within two business days after written agreement on the procedure and pass criteria. We propose shifting the coupon-dependent milestones, including the report due date, by two business days and continuing independent work as scheduled. Please confirm the custody and schedule terms, acceptance of the repeatability check, and the design limits the lab needs to finalize its proposal.

We accept the coupon custody and return terms, the two-mounting repeatability check, and a two-business-day shift for coupon-dependent milestones, including the report due date. Independent work may continue as scheduled. We’ll deliver the coupon within two business days after written agreement on the procedure and pass criteria.

For the shop, we propose limiting the tolerance table to mounting-interface characteristics needed to machine the fixture, such as hole sizes and spacing, mounting-face flatness, and seating dimensions. Our engineer will specify the permitted characteristics, nominal values, and tolerances in the table we approve for release to the named machinists. The test lead may check those characteristics against the coupon. The shop may reuse the stock already cut if it can finish the fixture using only the approved table and the finished fixture passes verification. The coupon stays at the Testing House, and the table will exclude page 4 geometry.

We’ll provide the lab with the coupon’s permitted excitation by axis and frequency, the applicable test band, and the fixture response limits for that band so it can propose the sweep level and maximum run-to-run difference. Both parties must approve the procedure and numerical criteria before either sweep. The lab will sign the results for both mountings, and prototype testing may begin once both parties sign off on a pass. Any fixture adjustment requires a fresh two-mounting check.

We propose replacing the blanket approval requirement with the following terms.

- **Trial data.** Raw failure traces and firmware parameters are confidential and may be accessed only by designated members of the parties’ trial teams. Both teams may use other trial measurements internally to run and evaluate the trial, with access limited to personnel who need them for that work.
- **External reports.** Either party may publish aggregate uptime across all three depots, provided the report omits route and depot identifiers and avoids breakdowns that would let readers infer them. The publishing party will give the other party 10 working days to review the draft. If no specific confidentiality concern is raised within that period, publication may proceed. If a concern is raised, the publishing party may proceed once it removes or resolves the material at issue. Other external disclosures of confidential trial data require prior written approval, subject to the safety exception below.
- **Urgent safety.** Either party may disclose the minimum information needed to address an imminent safety risk without prior approval. It will notify the other party as soon as practicable afterward, identifying what was shared and with whom.

What work will the external maintenance contractor perform during the trial? Could it do that work using fault summaries and diagnostic findings from the trial team? If there’s a specific task that requires a raw trace, please identify the task, the fields needed, and why a summary would be insufficient.

The contractor will diagnose faults, repair or replace affected units, and verify that they work before they return to service. We can start with a diagnostic summary containing the unit identifier, fault codes, relevant readings, and the sequence of events expressed in elapsed time. If the summary leaves the cause unclear, the operator’s technical lead can authorize a limited trace excerpt for that repair. For example, distinguishing a brief power interruption from a sensor fault may require the voltage and sensor readings in sequence around the failure. The contractor would receive only the channels and time window needed, under written confidentiality and repair-only use obligations, with access limited to assigned technicians and the excerpt deleted when the repair is closed. Can we make that a standing permission under the NDA, with each release logged by our technical lead?

For routine reporting, our trial lead will prepare a monthly board report covering combined uptime, fault counts, and repair status across the three depots. The operator can circulate that report to the board and its support staff on a confidential basis without further clearance. Board reports and public drafts will omit depot and route identifiers, exact timestamps, and breakdowns that could identify a depot or employee. If the board report will be made public, the publication terms apply.

Your 10-working-day review works for publication of combined uptime. The publishing party’s designated lead approves release after the review period if no specific confidentiality concern is raised. If a concern is raised, the lead may release the draft once the disputed material has been removed or both parties’ designated leads agree in writing on how to address it. Publication of other confidential trial data requires both parties’ written approval.

The safety exception also needs to cover prompt reporting of serious incidents to the appropriate authorities, including when the immediate danger has passed. Either party’s safety lead may make those reports, or disclose information needed to address an imminent risk, without prior notice or approval. The disclosure is limited to what the authority requires or what is reasonably needed for the safety response. For the first batch, may our external color specialist view the master images in a controlled workspace? Seeing the whole page helps them assess color across the sheet. We would identify the specialist for your written approval before granting access, bind them to the same confidentiality terms, disable downloads, and revoke access when calibration ends or the first batch is delivered, whichever comes first. If full-page access is unacceptable, we can provide archive-approved crops showing paper and ink, with the studio checking the results against the masters.

We propose limiting studio access to assigned scanning and quality-control staff. For each batch, we would keep working files for ten calendar days after delivery so you can flag corrections. On day ten, we would delete active copies except for scans with an open correction request, which we would delete upon redelivery. Encrypted backup copies would expire within 45 calendar days of active deletion. Only backup administrators could access them for disaster recovery, and we would reapply deletions after any restore.

We would like to publish one anonymized process image showing the scanning setup, with no legible correspondence, names, or identifying marks. We would submit the exact image, caption, and proposed publication channel for your written consent before use. Would that scope work for the archive?

We can agree to the following terms for the signed schedule.

- **Specialist access.** The first-batch specialist may use a full-page calibration sheet supplied by the archive. For the two restricted collections, the studio must keep all donor images, including crops, from external specialists and other subcontractors. For other collections, we can approve masked images or crops showing paper and ink. The archive must approve both the exact images and the named specialist in writing before access. We accept your confidentiality, download and access-expiry controls. Assigned studio scanning and quality-control staff can check the results against the masters.
- **Retention and deletion.** We accept ten calendar days after each batch delivery for corrections. Delete active copies on day ten, retaining only the scans needed for an open correction, and delete those upon redelivery. We propose a maximum of 30 calendar days from active deletion for encrypted backups, with your administrator-only disaster-recovery access and reapplication of deletions after any restore. Please provide a written record for each batch stating the active deletion date, any outstanding correction files and their eventual deletion dates, and confirmation when the last backup copy expires.
- **Incident contact.** Before transfer, each party will enter a named incident lead, monitored email address and telephone number in the schedule. The studio will notify the archive lead promptly and within 24 hours of discovering suspected unauthorized access, disclosure or loss, even if the investigation is ongoing. Include the affected materials and containment steps known at the time, then update us as facts emerge.
- **Publicity.** We can consider one photograph of the equipment with all donor materials out of frame and screens blank. Publication requires prior written archive approval of the exact photograph, caption and channel. Any change requires fresh approval.

Can you meet the 30-day backup limit? If your backup cycle requires 45 days, please identify that as an outstanding exception for express archive approval before transfer.

Our backups rotate on a 45-day cycle, so we cannot meet the proposed 30-day limit. **The backup period is the sole outstanding exception.** Please confirm in writing before transfer whether the archive approves a maximum of 45 calendar days from each file’s active deletion for its last encrypted backup copy to expire. We will hold transfer pending that approval.

We accept the ten-day correction window and the proposed batch deletion record. For scans retained for an open correction, the 45 days would run from deletion upon redelivery. We will confirm in writing when the last backup copy for each batch expires. Only backup administrators may access backups for disaster recovery, and we will reapply deletions after any restore.

We accept the specialist controls. The specialist may use the archive’s full-page calibration sheet. For the two restricted collections, all donor images, including crops, will stay with assigned studio staff. For other collections, we will obtain written archive approval of the named specialist and exact masked images or crops before granting access.

We also accept the incident-contact and notification terms and the publicity restriction. We will submit the exact equipment photograph, caption, and channel for written approval, with donor materials out of frame and screens blank. Any change will require fresh approval.

The archive approves the **45-calendar-day backup exception** for this pilot. For each file, the last encrypted backup copy must expire within 45 calendar days of active deletion. For a scan held for an open correction, that period starts when the studio deletes the active copy upon redelivery. A restore does not restart the clock.

Please record this limit in the signed schedule alongside the agreed access, retention, deletion-record, incident and publicity terms. No exceptions remain outstanding. Transfer may proceed once both parties have signed the schedule with their incident contacts filled in.

The first masked test obscured an ink-tone feature we need to verify. Before signature, would the archive approve a single supervised, on-premises review of one unmasked, nonrestricted sample? We would submit the exact image and specialist’s name for written approval. An assigned studio operator would display the image, retain control of the workstation, and close it at the end of the session. The specialist could take no photographs or copies. If the archive prefers, we can first try a revised crop that preserves the feature and submit that exact crop for approval. Both restricted collections remain excluded from specialist review.

For an open correction, we propose an acceptance test **before redelivery**. The operator would compare the rescan with the original letter under the agreed viewing conditions, verify that the ink-tone feature is distinguishable and that the requested correction is complete, and record the result in the batch log. A failed check would keep only the affected scan open for rework. A pass would trigger redelivery and deletion of the working copy upon redelivery, preserving the agreed backup deadline.

Would the archive accept the operator’s documented pass as sufficient for redelivery, and which sample-review option does it approve in principle?

We approve in principle one supervised review of the **physical comparison sheet at the archive**. We can offer one morning next week. Please send the specialist’s name and availability so we can confirm the appointment and the exact sheet in writing. The conservator will supervise. The specialist may inspect the ink-tone feature and advise on calibration. Only an archive-approved masked image of the comparison sheet may leave the archive. No photography or copying is permitted, and specialist review excludes donor letters and their images from every collection.

The studio may run calibration tests once the schedule is signed. We propose that the conservator validate color against the comparison original and record approval before first-batch donor scanning begins. If a revised masked crop shows the feature clearly enough for the conservator to validate the calibration, we can release scanning without waiting for the appointment.

**For corrections, we accept the assigned operator’s documented pass as sufficient for redelivery.** The operator will compare the rescan with the original under the agreed viewing conditions and record that the feature is distinguishable and the requested correction is complete. A failed check keeps only the affected scan open. Delete active batch files on day ten after delivery except for open corrections, and delete each corrected working copy upon redelivery. The last encrypted backup of each file must expire within 45 calendar days of its active deletion. Record the deletion dates and confirm final backup expiry in writing for each batch.

Please confirm the conservator’s first-batch approval role and the revised specialist scope for the signed schedule.

We agree to the revised terms for the signed schedule. After signature, the studio may run calibration tests. First-batch donor scanning will begin only after the conservator validates the color against the physical comparison original and records approval. We will try the revised masked crop first. If it preserves the ink-tone feature well enough for the conservator to approve calibration, scanning may proceed without the appointment.

If an in-person review is needed, we will provide the specialist’s name and availability so the archive can confirm the appointment and exact sheet in writing. The specialist may inspect only that physical comparison sheet at the archive, under the conservator’s supervision, and advise on calibration. Photography and copying are prohibited. Only an archive-approved masked image of the sheet may leave the archive. Donor letters and their images from every collection are excluded from specialist review.

We accept the correction procedure as written. The operator’s documented pass authorizes redelivery, and we will delete the corrected working copy upon redelivery.
